title: Examination practice · C Scope Circuit · Scope trace synthesis · variation 3
theme: Sand Dunes – Caravan Camp: a caravan camp

points: File-scope variables are declared outside functions; block-scope locals are visible in their block.
An inner declaration can hide an outer name. Leaving its scope restores the outer declaration.
Scope differs from lifetime: ordinary automatic locals belong to a block execution; file-scope objects have static storage duration.
lesson.title: Local and Global Variables

objective: Week 8 examination practice: Build 4 parallel branches, merge every branch by SUM, and feed the merged signal back for 3 passes before the output probe. In the scope controller, restore global visibility after a local block. Print the scope trace [15, 6], then send the incoming signal with writeOutput(signal) into the broadcast splitter. Final file-scope values: {'steps': 6}. Pass all 3 signal tests.
hint: Wire every splitter branch into the SUM merger. The feedback controller repeats the merged signal for the required pass count, then sends it to the probe. Declare globals before main. Braces create local scopes; an inner declaration hides an outer name until its block ends. Use Step to inspect the variable scopes and output trace.
controls: Drag components and connect pins. A splitter broadcasts a copy to every branch; the SUM merger waits for one result from each branch in the same pass. LOOP sends intermediate results back to split, and the final result to output. Select Program node to edit each C controller. Run tests every case; Step highlights the active node, wire and C line. Each node invocation starts fresh C scopes. Feedback passes and execution are bounded. readInput and writeOutput are bounded LogiCade helpers from logicade.h, not standard C functions.
